Now, the document that we're looking at here, Witness, is a situation report by the British military attache to Belgrade reporting an armed engagement around Baballoq on the 22nd of April. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we look at the summary: "FRY warned" -- that is, warned by the British government -- "of concern at reported Yugoslav Army involvement in fighting around Babaloc on the 22nd of April." And then under "detail": "Telecons under reference discussed media reports of fighting around Babaloc" -- and location is given -- "in which the Yugoslav Army was said to be involved, and our grounds for considering them credible. It was agreed that I should immediately warn the FRY of our concern." If we just pass --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could just pass over paragraph 3, which describes the conversation with the chef de cabinet and pick it up at paragraph 4: "First secretary (in Pristina) has subsequently talked to a number of journalists reporting events. There are conflicting views with some believing army and special forces are involved, others maintaining there is no direct evidence of this. It appears that Serb forces (of whatever composition) in the area were reinforced yesterday, with a position established on the hill overlooking the village. Today Albanians reacted, leading to exchanges of fire, possibly including mortars." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we're just waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, obviously you can see this document is dated the 22nd of April, but it refers to events that took place prior to that, including a specific influx and exchange the day before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 21st, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Is this the armed engagement that you were describing to us earlier on, do you think?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except here there is not that side that I was told about shooting on the 19th, on the Easter, from Babaloc side towards the settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it's true that some of the Albanian refugees mentioned military planes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military planes appearing in the area, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So -- so just to return to Judge Orie's question. I mean, you've had certain impressions given to you by Serb civilians.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Including, for example, an impression given you about an incident that took place at the Baballoq refugee camp on the 28th of April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But -- but does it appear to you clear that there were armed engagements taking place between fairly considerable Serbian military forces and forces on the other side during this period in April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, starting from 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you don't know where the Serb forces were based in relation to the Baballoq refugee camp at that point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except what Albanian refugees told and what Serbian refugees said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the Albanians told you they were in the refugee camp shooting from there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the Serbian refugees told you they were patrolling in the area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only that, but it was conflicting also in the dates because Serbian refugees said that actually Albanian KLA forces are on the Suka e Babaloc at 18th night and 19th in the morning and during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they also mentioned in Katik [phoen] the roads that night between 19th and 20th so that the KLA controlled the Decani-Djakovica road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So a fairly conflicting picture --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- but some significant armed engagements taking place on both sides?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one or two other matters, if I may, briefly with you. You -- from paragraph 78 onwards describe certain matters concerning the arrival of the FARK. And just to understand the basis for your recollection, you indicate in paragraph 78 that you think that they arrived around May.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And a little further on, you describe - bear with me a moment - a situation that arose in Isnic which led to the evacuation --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- of civilians and FARK troops, which you describe as having taken place in July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was July, in the summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, you don't have any records of these -- of the information or the sources of your information for this, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. I mean, it -- you could -- would you accept you could be out by several months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For -- you mean for the summer for the refugees or for -- for FARK?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For the arrival of FARK and the issues that you're describing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, because I think that the same period, in the end of April, there was a big funeral, again, in Erec and it was a big political event.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, we may be at cross-purposes here. Before you -- before you carry on, I'm asking you about the dates that you've given here in relation, first of all, to the arrival --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I'm explaining --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to explain why I think it happened in May, because in March and April LDK still didn't know how to deal with KLA appearance and the fights. And by the end of April on that big funeral, big political names appeared and -- in Erec and there was kind of popular invitation for the -- for uprising.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's, I think, that's in my head now is that somehow then FARK appears together.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Would you accept that their arrival in Kosovo could have been as late as the last week of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that they arrived so late.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand probing the sources and accuracy of your information. And the incident in Isnic where Vukmir Mrksic delivered an ultimatum for the surrender of weapons. You put that in July. Could that have been as late as September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really. It was summer. It was time when Orahovac also was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally in paragraph 82, you -- you describe the decision of Tahir Zemaj to surrender weapons, and so forth. And you -- you refer to Albanians that you interviewed later.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Telling you what Ramush Haradinaj thought about that decision. First of all, can you tell us, please, the names of the people, if you know them, who gave you that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is really basically hearsay. I don't think that I can at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's -- that's quite important --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- for us to understand that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, because really -- and that's what I also said to the Prosecutor why I think my -- my testimony was not of great importance. I mean, I was not a witness of the crimes or victim of the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, just --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the fact is that it was talk in Balkan way. You do some things, you hear the other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we take it, please, then that what you have recorded here as having been a -- a statement of Mr. Haradinaj's position is really nothing more than rumour or gossip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I don't know what he really said, and I'm not sure even that these people who told me that were witness, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: I don't -- I think we'll probably be able -- we'll be close to the normal --

utterances.text: We'll be close to our normal time, in any event.

utterances.text: I shall be brief.

utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Witness 28, you mentioned early in your testimony today that you relied on a number of sources for the information that you were compiling, and so I'm clear, was one of those sources the Council for the Defence of Human Rights and Freedoms in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, if -- if you would not mind that I interrupt you for a moment I just received an urgent request. I have to break at 5.30. So therefore we'll have a break at 5.30. I apologise, but I wasn't aware of that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH

utterances.text: -- two minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we -- if we could, starting on page 1 in the comment section of that - and by that I mean the very first paragraph before it discusses the events in the Drenica region and surround -.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you aware of the arrest of Rasim Muhamet Selmanaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Later was tried also by Serbian court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could turn now to page 2, the date being the 27th of March, under the title of "Shtime." utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't find this part of the report. No, for this case, I can't recollect. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. In -- in March of 1998, there were a series of demonstrations that were still occurring throughout Kosovo which were peaceful demonstrations, as they could be called, where -- whereby Albanian individuals were protesting against what they perceived to be Serbian, let's say, abuses, aggression, or otherwise mistreatment? Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Protests -- I actually was there when the protests occurred, and they've been -- they occurred after the Prekaz event. I think women also protested and students for the -- for the massacre that happened in Prekaz, if it is that protest we are talking in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And after the protest in March, did you become aware of the fact that the protesters or any of the protesters were arrested by the Serbian police for their peaceful protest activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do think that we covered this arrests. I can't recollect now specific cases, but we do -- we did follow that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you learn whether or not any of those protesters, after having been arrested, suffered any injuries as a result of having been arrested and being imprisoned for whatever period of time they were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I just can say that I would expect them to be probably beaten in arrest, but I really can't remember specific name now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, if you can't remember a specific name, that's fine, then. I understand your general attitude about the situation. Continuing with this report, on the 28th of March it indicates that a plane of armed forces of the Yugoslav Army flew very low over the Gjakova territory in the area on the border with Albania. At about 12 p.m. a convoy of military and police forces from Gjakova was situated in Kodra e Hasit village, seven kilometres away from the town."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were -- was your organisation aware of -- of those kinds of mobilisations, specifically this mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have been receiving reports and interviewing people who were fleeing the border zone toward Djakovica, and there were frequent reports about military stopping the smuggling of the weapons and also some people were missing. A couple reports about missing people we did put together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And one -- and one last question before we take the break. These reports were reports, if I -- if I understood your testimony correctly that, you received on a daily basis. You were getting the information contemporaneously as these events were unfolding.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from KIC, and they record this and we followed these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could take the break at this point.

utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could indicate, it is unlikely that I will have more than one question for this witness, and so Mr. Guy-Smith might be entitled to a slight -- a larger slice of the pie than that, but -- with respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Harvey. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One of the things that was -- was occurring, of course, was that apart from getting the daily information, there was also delayed information that was coming in to -- to you, in terms of the kinds of things that were occurring on the ground during this period of time; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I quite didn't understand this. Can you repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely. Apart from receiving information on a daily basis, also what was happening was you were receiving some information concerning events that had occurred earlier and you got the information a little bit later, later in the week, for example.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later in the week, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And in -- for example - I'm looking at page 3, and I'm still dealing with the very -- the very same report, that's report number 402, under "Delayed information." If you go down to the - one, two, three - it's the third paragraph from the bottom. It says: "On 19 March, after the Albanians' peaceful protest, some armed Serbs chased some students with the" -- and then names the gymnasium -- "and forced them to jump into the Drini i Bardhe River." And my question to you is -- do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question to you there is: Essentially what was happening at this period of time was, not only was there increased tensions as between the -- the Albanian civilians and the police but there was also increased tensions between Serbian civilians and Albanian civilians during that period of time because of what was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. This is -- only -- 'cause Serbs had all positions in the towns and control all positions while in the villages Serbs were minority and as such had actually a difficult time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. If we could now move to the next report, which is report number 403, which is 2D1110. And if we could get a MFI number for that, please, I'd appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as D196.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could, I'd like to -- I'd like to jump to page -- to page 2, dealing with the date of April 2nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And on April 2nd, it indicates under "Mitrovica" -- could we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first wait until it's -- no, it's -- the witness has a copy, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Under "Mitrovica" it says: "The police check-points at Qipol [phoen], Turnovac [phoen] and Kline e Eperme were reinforced." Are those check-points that you had gone through that were Serbian check-points while you were traveling in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, they were check-points surrounding basically Drenica region, Glogovac, Mitrovica, and Srbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now moving to April 4th, it indicates, under "Skenderaj," that: "At 5 a.m. the village of Lausha was shelled from different kinds of weapons." Were you aware of that shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've been aware and we interviewed many of the villagers of Dreznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And finally on that same page, page 2, it says "The events in the district of Decan." And if you go down from the first line of "Decan," one, two, three -- to the fourth line that says: "The gravest situation is in the villages of Gllogjan, Dubrave, Shaptej, and Prekolluke or" --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prekolluke.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Prekolluke. Were you aware of --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't see this. Where is that? April?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yeah, under -- under "The events in the district of Decan."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And what -- what is the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The date is still under April 4th. And if you go down from where it says -- it has the word "Decan." You go, one, two, three, four lines down. The sentence starts with the word: "The gravest situation is in the villages of Gllogjan, Dubrave ..." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was that something you were aware of at the time it occurred, on April 4th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on April 4th. I was aware that Hime Haradinaj was buried and that he died in the forest wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Moving on to the -- the next page. And it seems that we're going back in time, in terms of dates. And if we could look at the date of March 30th and March 31st. You had mentioned that people were summoned for informative talks and you explained to the Chamber what informative talks were. I'd like you to take a look, first of all, at March 30th under the area of Prizren. It indicates on the second line that Isa Berisha (1972) which I'm guessing was his birth date, "was once again summoned to the police under the pretext of being a member of the KLA. He was ordered to report again on April 6th. He was physically ill-treated." Then on March 31st, under the line of Kacanik, it indicates that a gentleman was summoned for informative talks in order to report again, and the same thing happened to a Haki Baxhrimaj [phoen], who, I believe, was born in 1943 in Giljan, he was also summoned for informative talks. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This cases I can't recognise. We didn't investigate this cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. But --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We actually couldn't cope with so many different abuses, so we had to basically pick several cases that we could then in -- and in-depth research.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood. With regard to the language used of "informative talks," was that a phrase that was used by not only your group but also by this group to describe a particular kind of summoning of an individual by the police to the police station with -- with the resultant things that you've told us about, including the beatings and other abuses? So it was understood that when you saw that language, "informative talks," that there was some concern about there being some kind of human rights abuse with regard to that individual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 5 of the same document, under "Delayed information." In Kline and -- I'm -- it says: "On March 5th, Mark Oroshi (1959) from the village of Leskoc, an activist of the LDK, was summoned to the Serbian-run District Court in Klina." Now, by this time - and by that I mean in April - the LDK was engaged in what was generally considered to be still a peaceful attempt at resolution, was it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, you're developing a speed which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood. I'll slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you have my question in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe at that point, as I can remember the political situation, Serbs -- Serbian regime didn't really make the difference between KLA and LDK, so everything was put on the back of LDK what was happening with different KLA activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. This gentleman was summoned to the Serbian-run District Court in Klina. He was arrested and severely ill-treated for allegedly being an associate of the KLA. Police threatened to cut his genital organs. Due to injuries suffered, he had to seek for medical help. On March 16th, he was once again taken to court. Are you aware of this particular case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular case, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At the -- there are a number other instances --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, can you slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I can. My concern is -- my concern quite frankly is this, Your Honour. I'm looking -- I'm looking at the clock, and I am in the second of 23 reports and I want to get through them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [French spoken] And I have now turned to the French channel in order to work with the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just in terms of scheduling, we do have another witness here at the moment. Could I just inform the Trial Chamber and the parties the witness has made some minor changes to his proposed Rule 92 ter statement, and they're in the process of being translated. Now, Mr. Di Fazio said he could either inform the Defence orally of what these are and give them a copy of it or start with the witness orally, if we get to him, or start in the morning. Those are the options at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Looking at our schedule for the coming days and the coming weeks, I'd rather not lose even a minute in court; although, I'm aware that the Chamber today have stolen -- has stolen also some time, but there were good reasons for that. Mr. Guy-Smith, even with -- at the French speed, how much time would you think you would still need? Another ten minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that realistically I will be at least another 20 to 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you need in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll probably need about five minutes. But just in relation to the next witness. Could I say that he actually arrived at our office at about 4.00, having been delayed at the airport. So we didn't actually get to speak to him until 4.00 p.m. and have made all efforts to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry to rise, I'm just slightly puzzled because I'm not aware of the Prosecution having served a 92 ter statement for this next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, it's his statement. We would have just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: His statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We would just seek to adopt it, that's all. What we were only -- we were just going to rely upon that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the February 2006 statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, if it is proposed that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that we at this moment do not take any final decision on whether we could continue and certainly not bother Witness 28 with our procedural discussions. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could now -- now turn to the next report, number 406, which is 2D1101. And if we could have an MFI number, I'd appreciate it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as D197.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could now turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this is with regard to events of April 21st discussing what was occurring in Decan. It states: "At 10.45 a.m. Serbian police and military forces attacked with artillery and mortars the village of Baballoq. Serbian forces accompanied with armoured cars were stationed at the Suka e Baballocit and in the vicinity of the refugee settlement." It also says in the same paragraph, and I'm deleting some of the language: "The villagers are making attempts to organise their defence." Now, with regard to the villages organising a defence, I take it that what they're referring to here - if you know - are the Albanian villagers in the villages of, for example, Likoshan, Qirez, Prekaze, where you have civilian Albanians who out of a concern of what is occurring with these Serbian military forces are doing their best to figure a way of defending their homes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of these events was slightly different but, again, I'm basing that on different testimonies. I actually think that there was attack on Babaloc settlement on 18th/19th, and then after that military forces -- Serbian military forces -- and as you can see, it's mentioned military planes that also many of the villagers said, returned attack and suppressed that. So at that point, probably on 21st, it's true as it is said. I'm not quite sure was that just defence of the villagers at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And going on to the next day, the 22nd, under "Decan." It indicates that: "Since the early hours of the morning, police and military forces from Radoniqi Lake, the villages of Palabaldh and Boka and the refugee settlement in Baballoq have been shelling Suka e Babollocit and Baballoq itself." Now, my question here is: Is by -- by this time in April, had you become aware of the extensive use of shelling by the Serbian police and other forces of these villages? And by that I mean villages which were inhabited by Albanian civilians.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Albanian refugees were talking about these shellings. I am not sure that military forces were Radonjic Lake. I just heard that they were on Suka Babaloc and not in Babaloc itself. In the Suka Crmljanska, while all other villages were basically under control of KLA. That was my understanding at the time. But yes, they were shelling the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the villages that were being bombarded were villages in which there was a -- an extensive civilian population that -- that may or may not have been supporting the -- the basic ideas of the KLA. They were fellow travelers, you could say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's possible. That's possible. Because I never encountered Serbian police making a real difference between civilians or KLA or supporters of KLA. They usually just didn't mind -- thought it was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe last week you mentioned an individual by the name of Arkan.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'd like to refer you to page 7 of this document. And under the heading of "Prishtina" it says: "Four military trucks full of soldiers paraded through the Jabllanice road in Kodra e Trimave. Arkan was seen in Hajvalia during a visit to the Serbian special police units."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard numerous times that Arkan's troops are coming and Arkan's troops are there. I actually don't think that Arkan was ever in Kosovo, that his units at that point were not interfering there. I just think it was different units. Different units and different paramilitary troops. Not nicer. But I just think that many Albanian villagers just by the pure fact that "Arkan" meant something very nasty, as he was, was -- they were always thinking that Arkan is coming or describing the Arkan units there. I -- I was not aware that Arkan was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: For a moment, if I could, you said "different units and different paramilitary troops." I take it that during your research what you did learn during that time independent of your belief of whether or not it was Arkan himself who was in Kosovo, was that there were other paramilitary troops who were operating in the region at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. If we clarify what "paramilitaries" really mean, because I believe that they were controlled by the -- by the centre in Belgrade, so there was no ad hoc at that point. Maybe later during the bombardment. But in 1998 there was no ad hoc forces that would come just there and do -- do whatever they want. They've been controlled. I knew for two. One was called Lightning, Munja, and that was from Pec. And I heard -- I seen this Sheshirdzije, as they were called. I don't know how to translate that in English really. Somebody who wears the hat. And I seen them as such. But I did believe they were special forces -- different kind of special forces. I'm not military expert. So I don't know more about that, let's say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to turn to page 9 of the same document, if I could. And looking under the line item where it says "Gjilan," at the very last sentence of that, it indicates that: "On April 18th, Serbian forces in the prison of Gjilan demanded from Albanian prisoners to vote on the forthcoming referendum of April 23rd." First of all, do you remember the referendum of April 23rd, what that was about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was referendum that Milosevic government opened for not interference of International Community into internal affairs. I think that it was that. And I don't know for this case specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did -- did you or your organisation ever receive any information that those people who were detained in Serbian prisons were being forced to vote in any particular kind of a way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. If we could return to the next -- I'm sorry, if we could go to the next report, which is 2D1122, report number 408. I have just been corrected. It should be 2D001122. If I could have an MFI number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be marked for identification number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D198, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the -- during the time that you were involved in your research, did you learn of the Serbian military using bright lights at night as a form of either intimidating the population or, I would say, panicking the population? And I'm referring to, if you could look at page 2 under "May 1st." And it's -- it's well down under "Decan," right before the paragraph is over. And it has the name of Halil Imer Lokaj. But my interest is the following sentence: "During the night, military forces are pointing their reflectors towards houses in order to cause panic. Fire was opened in the direction of the village of Baballoq." We've had testimony that Serbian forces saw lights at night in the area which -- which they attributed to the KLA. And my question to you is: Did you ever receive any information that -- that the Serbian forces were using this particular form of warfare with the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I also note that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- I don't recall this specific allegation being put, as should have been put under Rule -- Rule 90(H), to the witness, I think with Mr. Rade Repic, who gave this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meaning that Mr. Guy-Smith would have to put his case to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Meaning that. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's right. If indeed it's the case of the Defence that those lights were the Serbian forces, that should have been put to the relevant witnesses at the relevant time. I just note that in passing so it could be put at the relevant point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since this witness -- this witness is not aware of anything of the kind, let's proceed. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I -- I note Mr. -- I note Mr. Re's objection, and I'm sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At a point during this we're going to be dealing with issues of what's good for the goose is good for the gander in a variety of areas with regard to Prosecution, but we'll deal with that at another point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's leave it for that moment, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we now turn to point number 414 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] If I could have an MFI number for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could now return to report number 414, 2D001094. If we could have a MFI number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be D199.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'd like to direct your attention to the 21st of May, under "Decan," where it indicates the following: "The situation in the district of Decan continues to be grave. There was shooting and shelling towards the village of Baballoq. The town continues to be blocked. Police and military forces are parading through the town in a show of power. The situation is very grave -- especially is" -- I'm sorry, excuse me. "The situation is very grave, especially in the villages on the border with Albania and Junik. Armed refugees are participating in the attacks against the Albanian villages." During the -- your research, did you become aware of a programme from Belgrade where all Serbian men were to be reserve army fighters and were issued weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not really even Milosevic invention. That was Communist country, so all base of Yugoslav Army was that every person, civilian, has to go to the army and stays being a reservist all the way through until he's, like, 55, I think, or something like that. So that was kind of Yugoslav law. And I -- I was aware that there were -- that there was attempt to arm Serbian civilians beginning of the March mostly in the villages where they been really nervous about attacks, and I was also aware that Serbian police very often didn't actually help when they really came under attack. Like, for example, in Klina municipality. So they would pull out, a little bit defend themselves and then surrender and escape. And Serbian police wasn't -- didn't have at that time power to enter and do anything. It was May, May when these events were happening. Mostly in Klina, with the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. In the -- going -- in the same document, looking at May 22nd, under "Peja," it indicates that "Large police forces armed with heavy weaponry were stationed on the hill over the villages of Gllogjan and Nepole." Were you aware of -- of that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about the Glodjane in Decani municipality? I was not aware of that information, and I actually doubt that it's true. I think it's first time really when Serbian police entered Rznic and Glodjane was the end of August when they launched big offensive. They did try to launch, I think, nine offensives into Rznic and Glodjane, but they never really entered the -- the space, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, just so we're clear, this is information - and by that I mean you were receiving, as I understood it, the -- the daily reports, the KIC reports, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: KIC. And we were then but also that report needs to be double-checked in a -- in a way. So I was not aware of that ever since, basically, after 25th of April to the end of August any police forces entered Glodjane. I don't doubt. I don't say it's true. I just say I was not aware. I'm surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With -- with that in mind, then, turning to page -- page 4, dealing with the date of May 23rd, once again in Decan, it indicates: "Large police forces were stationed on the cross-road near Prejlep on the road Decan-Gjakova. They opened fire towards the villages of Prejlep and Dranoc. The situation is very dramatic. 20 APCs, 2 armoured cars, 2 cannons, and large police forces made efforts to pass through the villages of Carrabreg i Poshtem and Prejlep, but they clashed with the forces of the KLA."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding was from May 23rd to May 31st, when actually the fighting really started, that Serbian police and army mounted presence there, as well as probably the other side was getting ready for the clash over these -- controlling the road and opening toward the border. That was my understanding what was happening at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Pardon. We didn't really understand. The beginning of your answer was: "My understanding was from May 23rd to May 21st."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 31st. 31st, sorry, three-one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: To May 31st. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Turning to 2D001134, report number 416. If I could have a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- MFI number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D200, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could go down to the -- it's right in about the middle of the page. It says -- starts with the language, on the second time, it says: "On May 31st, the situations in the villages in the district of Decan, as well as in the neighbouring villages is dramatic. A war is fought between Serbian police, military, and paramilitary forces and Albanian villagers."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's true. On May 31st in the morning started a real battle between Serbian police. I would not say -- call that any more "Albanian villagers." I really think it was KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you -- when you say that you really think it's -- it's the KLA, did -- did you have at that time information that there were villagers who were also at that time fighting, apart from the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- my understanding of KLA at that time was that there was not too many soldiers, so it was not powerful army but had support -- supports from the villagers and -- who basically joined because of belief in that way of fights and future of Kosovo or because they just got armed in fear of Serbian revenge. But it was a mix of the villagers, armed villagers, and KLA soldiers. Conscripts, I would say. KLA. 'Cause as far as I remember, it lasted more than seven days and the media were forbidden to enter the -- enter that zone at all -- at all. And it was after that in Decani many houses were burnt. It was quite a stressful time for all civilians there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And -- and during that time, was the Mother Teresa foundation was working in the area, was it not, in an attempt to bring aid to civilians who were suffering from what was occurring at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I remember Mother Teresa, yeah, working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That last question, relevance, Mr. Guy-Smith, becomes more and more a question to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There has been discussion about doctors being stopped and being disallowed to give aid. And to the extent that this is something that occurred here and people who were in that position --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please ask about what you're referring to as a relevant issue. I take it that you can't -- you can't frustrate the work of doctors if there are no doctors. That's for sure. That's -- but let's come to your point, if there's any specific issue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Turning to page 7 of the same document, under the line of "Peja." This is, once again, for the date of May 31st. Were you aware of there being clashes in the villages of -- of Raushiq?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I thought that Rausic was later in the summer had clashes with -- with military.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. If we could go to the next report, report number 418, 2001156?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It needs a number, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D201, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to point your attention now to page 2, under "Prishtina." Were you aware of the fact that there was an -- an increased number of soldiers coming into the region -- and I'm reading specifically the following: "Six cars with reservists and three covered cars probably with weapons arrived at the railway station in Fushe-Kosova at about 10 a.m. Over 1000 Serbian soldiers arrived at the railway station in Prishtine."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you remind me of the date. The date, can you remind me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: June 8th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: June 8th. In Pristina now? I can't remember seeing military presence in Pristina. Yes, in Pec, not in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Turning to page 3 on June 9th under "Gjakova." There's an indication that "The villages of Reka e Keqe and other villages in the district of Decan were shelled from military bases in" -- and it names a number of them. "And Suka e Biteshit during the whole night. Today Skivan, from where the population has moved to other parts, was shelled. The shelling from Boka e Zhdrelle is towards the 'Radoniqi' hydrosystem, may damage the dam and so endanger the whole population of the Dukagjini plain. Large Serbian forces were concentrated in town and are checking all entrances and exits." Was that a concern of -- that your organisation was is that these Serbs were going to flood the plain by damaging the dam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say I never heard this. I actually don't think that they could do it, because as far as I know, Radonjic hydrosystem was in the back of the villages, that they actually didn't enter all the way until the end of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We have quite a few reports here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- which I'm not going to go through, but I'd like to ask you this: Because you've had an opportunity to see these reports and obtain the information on a daily basis. With regard to the Albanian civilians who were killed, is the information that you've -- you've seen in that regard that's contained in these reports accurate, as far as you're concerned, based upon your experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My experience was that the report was slightly avoiding to mention KLA and was slightly presenting always villagers fighting, which was not quite like that. When we tried to check what -- on the ground what they mentioned as abuse and torture prove -- was very often proven right and never was mention in these reports anything what was happening with the other -- I mean, minority at that point, Serbs. So I would say, yes, but was slightly twisted into the -- the situation that was suiting that for international media and creating the public opinion. Slightly. That was my feeling.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you know a gentleman who was a lawyer and a member of the board of the CDHRF named Destan Rukiqi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rukiqi, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could turn to D186, report number 426.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to -- to discuss with you the following. It's at the bottom of page 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, of course, I do not know what your next questions will be, but Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- did not gain the impression that that -- that a lot of -- going through these reports in such detail did greatly assist the Chamber. But, of course, since you are going back to one now, it might be different. We hope so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You had discussed earlier on issues concerning the judicial process with Mr. Emmerson. And my -- my question to you is: Is the information here, as far as you know, based on your research, accurate that Destan Rukiqi --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rukiqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. "A lawyer, member of the board of the CDHRF, was sentenced to 60 days of imprisonment and sent to serve his prison term. As Rukiqi was not allowed to examine the files on the case of his client, he accused Danica Marinkovic, a judge, the role of playing policeman." Are you aware of this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware. I think I can recollect there was this dispute. I'm not aware that he was sent 16 days in prison. But I know that there was a dispute. And I'm sorry to say I was not aware of that. Or maybe I was then, but I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, if possible, we'd like to finish with this witness today --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since there are ten minutes left. I'd invite you to wrap up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'll make it ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as -- as a matter of fact, what occurred with Mr. Rukiqi, if we could look at 2D001180, report number 427?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Needs a number, Mr. Guy-Smith, I take it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be marked for identification as D202, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Page 6, under the line of "Prishtina." "On being severely tortured in the county gaol in Prishtina, Destan Rukiqi, a lawyer and member of the board of the CDHRF in Prishtina, was taken to hospital. His health condition is qualified as very grave." Were you -- were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- no, no, I was not aware that he was really in the hospital. I was aware that there was a dispute and there was some kind of process.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You had mentioned earlier that there was some difficulties, I believe, with individuals having access to their families and their lawyers --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- once arrested.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could take a look at 2D001209 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Report number 429.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I earlier said that the Chamber did not feel that it's greatly assisted by the line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I've got French and English. I'm with now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That we felt that we're not greatly assisted by your line of questioning. Then I invited you to wrap up and said that we would have ten minutes left. Would you -- I mean, you are now asking for another document, to find out whether quite a lot of things -- where the witness was asked whether she's aware of it - sometimes she is, sometimes she is not - a lot of personal knowledge seems not to be there. That's -- You're not to be blamed for it, Witness 28.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's impossible to remember all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith, would you please finish your cross-examination within the next two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In terms of the information that you were receiving on a daily basis from this organisation, in summary would it be fair to say that you were receiving information concerning the death of Albanian citizens, the attacks on villages, the abrogation of a variety of legal rights from the period commencing in March through and including September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We have been. These reports were exactly pointing to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And these were reports that you relied upon in terms of making a determination of where to focus your efforts concerning human rights abuses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the sources that we --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That -- I understand, one of the sources, among others.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to one issue, Your Honour, I can ask her to identify the remaining reports. I believe that of all the reports, she might be in a position to identify the remaining reports, at which they can receive MFI numbers and at a later point in time, because of the shortness of time that exists, and then we can deal with the issue of their admission at a later point in time. However you choose to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, is there any -- what then exactly she would have to identify? This being reports? I think you just took her to these reports and asked the questions about it without specifically --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, she had earlier indicated that she had received the information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: She had received the information on a daily basis and on a weekly basis and recognised these reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Re, would there be any dispute about similar reports but then with other numbers and other information as being within the knowledge of the witness when she worked at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I -- I've got no idea. I've -- I have not asked the witness about all these individual reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Maybe yes, maybe no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you rely on these reports during whole of your time you were working in -- in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't rely. I was using that as a source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you were using as a source for focusing your attention.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's -- okay. Then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll later discuss, Mr. Guy-Smith, whether it -- these reports do assist, but one thing is for clear, that these kind of reports were used by the witness to focus her attention on certain matters. Mr. Harvey -- That will not be -- that will not be the issue in future.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There might be other issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right, there might be other issues. But I take it for the time being we'll get MFI numbers for the remainder of them so there's no question about which reports exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then please inform Mr. Re as soon as possible which -- what reports altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll see --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with that I am -- with that, I am done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: There is one of those reports for which I would like an MFI number, and that 2D001215, report number 428. While that's being brought up --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness 28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be D203.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And Witness 28, this gives me an opportunity to tell you that Mr. Harvey is counsel for Mr. Brahimaj. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That's just what I was about to tell you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down towards the bottom of that page, please. Thank you. A little bit further up. And a little further still. Lovely. Thank you very much. This document, again, do you recall the -- what is described at the top of the document as the widespread repression and harassment perpetrated by the Serbian police and other authorities in Kosovo from August 2nd until August 6th, 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't remember that being limited from 2nd to 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that middle July there was attempt of Serbian forces to suppress KLA existence in different villages. By then I think more than 40 per cent of territory was already controlled by KLA, as far as I can understand in the villages. So really what was happening, they would start pushing and bombarding the village by village. Refugees fleeing to the next -- the next municipality till we reached the point of real catastrophic situations. But I don't remember it being from between -- between 2nd to 6th. Maybe just for this municipality that was that situation ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I wanted just to focus on the period covered by this report. And we see at the -- towards the bottom of the page here, it says: "On July 4th to 5th," -- and I think you can probably agree with me that this must be a typographical error in the report. They were in fact speaking of the -- the August period here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So that should read "August 4th to 5th."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And it lists a number of people who were killed in Jabllanice e Dushkajes, near Decan. I don't know whether any of these names are familiar to you, but one of the factors that one does notice looking at this aspect of the report is the extreme age of the victims. I don't know if you have any knowledge at all of my client, Lahi Brahimaj. Do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So -- so you wouldn't be able to help on whether the Aze Ibrahimaj and the Zize Zekaj who are mentioned here are respectively his mother and grandmother [Realtime transcript read in error "brother"]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In relation then to Jabllanice which you do mention in paragraph 28 -- and I'm done with this document for now, thank you. In relation to paragraph 28 of your -- your 92 ter statement, you refer to a conversation that you had with an American TV crew.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And their investigations in Jabllanice where they found the local KLA commander who had a long white beard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think it's fairly evident that my client, try as he might, would have difficulty growing a long white beard. I'm not asking you to respond to that observation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I might also -- do you mind if I interrupt something about Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, may I -- may I finish my question first and then by all means add any comment that seems to you to be helpful. I wanted to ask you, since this description in fact fits that of a gentleman known as Sadri Zeneli, did you ever come-- become aware of Sadri Zeneli as being the local commander in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, by all means if you wish to add anything in relation to Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it's interesting -- is it open session? Yeah? Yeah? Yeah, maybe it's interesting to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this to say that you would like to remain in open session or that you would rather return --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, I think it should remain, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be interesting to know that me and the researcher that was mentioned earlier had been in May that year interviewing two people, a very old couple, Serbs, but who -- very difficulty talk Serbian. They were from Jablanica and already completely assimilated. And they told us that in January 1998 they've been ordered to leave Jablanica by unknown people they'd never seen before. They'd never had children and never were interested to actually leave that place. Their neighbours tried to protect them for -- for months. And then in the end the neighbours decided that they cannot protect them, so they put then flour and sugar on the truck and sent them. So we found them in May in Pec in the refugee centre. But that's the first time that I heard aside of this TV crew testimony about Jablanica and digging the trenches and seeing unknown faces in January 1998.
